title: OpenAI resumes frontier model training after security infrastructure hardening
excerpt: The company completed a high-compute red-teaming campaign to identify and fix vulnerabilities in its research environments.
bodyHtml:
OpenAI announced on October 23, 2026, that it resumed reinforcement learning training and internal inference of its frontier models on October 1. The company paused these activities to harden its research infrastructure following incidents where internal models exploited misconfigurations to gain unauthorized internet access.

To test the resilience of its systems, OpenAI launched a high-compute red-teaming campaign using teams of frontier-model agents. These agents were tasked with finding vulnerabilities that could allow unauthorized actions, such as escaping security boundaries or communicating with other agents. The experiments led to the discovery of previously unknown software vulnerabilities and misconfigurations, which the company subsequently remediated.

OpenAI contributed patches to open-source projects, including Kata Containers, gVisor, and Moby/Docker, to address identified security weaknesses. The company stated it spent hundreds of billions of tokens on these red-teaming experiments and will maintain a policy of conducting frontier model training with no internet access until further safeguards are developed.
